# RightDisplay Apple TV Helper — third-party notice

The helper uses zeroconf 0.150.0 under LGPL-2.1-or-later. Its complete pure-Python package is under `_internal/zeroconf/`; no zeroconf modules are placed in PYZ and no zeroconf Cython extensions are bundled by the current spec. Original LGPL terms are retained under Legal/LegacyLicenseMaterials/zeroconf-LGPL-2.1.txt; exact source is under Legal/CorrespondingSources/zeroconf-0.150.0.tar.gz.

You may exercise the library's original modification, replacement and debugging rights; no RNSL restriction is applied to the library itself. Replace the complete compatible `_internal/zeroconf/` package while the helper is stopped, or rebuild with the published source/spec/locks. Do not copy compiled extensions from a different ABI. Changes to a signed app may require your own valid local re-signing and operating-system approval; no official private key or official identity is provided or required for source compilation. Re-signing does not grant official endorsement.

Build scripts and exact dependency sources/hashes are in the source repository. `Scripts/build_helper.py` accepts explicit CPython3.12.14 arm64 and wheel inputs, enforces hash pins, builds pure Python zeroconf and removes build-only tools before packaging. A source release must retain first-party helper sources/spec/scripts, applicable dependency locks and corresponding third-party materials. Exact source references and source-delivery methods still need final distribution review.

Technical evidence: the real packaged executable loads a modified external zeroconf package during --help under network-denial. This does not establish behavior of a replacement inside a signed official app or close the legal question of RNSL restrictions on the combined work. The LGPL2.1 section6 rights for modification of the combined work for a customer's own use and reverse engineering must not be obstructed. Current RNSL section7.3 explicitly mentions Third-Party Components; whether that is sufficient for this combination requires legal confirmation. No first-party commercial rights are newly granted here.

CPython and each Python/native dependency retain their own terms. The CPython standalone native sources, notices and scope are recorded under standalone-20260825; cryptography's separate OpenSSL4.0.1 and Rust declarations are retained separately. A publisher dependency graph includes build tools and is not a claim that every crate is separately present at runtime.
